steps.description: Click the "Declarative Agent" option in the "New Project" popup within the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit interface to start creating an agent by declaring instructions.

Click the "No Action" option in the dropdown menu under "Add an action to your declarative agent" in the "Create Declarative Agent" dialog within Visual Studio Code using the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit extension.
Click the "Default folder" dropdown in the "Workspace Folder" dialog to set the project root folder path (`/home/.vscode/AgentsToolkitProjects`).
Press the F1 key to open the Command Palette in Visual Studio Code.
Type 'add capability' into the VS Code command palette input field at the top of the interface.
Click the "Microsoft 365 Agents: Add Capability" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette.
Click the "Web Search" option in the "Add Capability" dropdown menu within Visual Studio Code to select web search as the grounding information source.
Click the "Search by URL" option in the "Select Search Type" dropdown within Visual Studio Code.
Enter 'https://example.com' into the address input field in the "Web Content" dialog at the top of the Visual Studio Code window.
Press Enter to confirm the URL input ("https://example.com") in the "Web Content" address bar at the top of the Visual Studio Code interface.
Click the "manifest.json" file entry in the "Select Teams manifest.json File" dialog in Visual Studio Code.

Click the "Add" button in the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit confirmation dialog within Visual Studio Code. The button is centered at the top of the interface, enables toolkit modifications, and is visually indicated by a red crosshair.
Press the F1 key to open the Command Palette in the Visual Studio Code.
Type #text:'Notifications: Show Notifications' into the Visual Studio Code command palette input box at the top center of the window.
Click the "Notifications: Show Notifications" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette to select it.
Press Enter to select "Notifications: Show Notifications" in the VS Code command palette.

Click the "View agent manifest" button in the notification popup at the bottom-right corner of the Visual Studio Code interface, confirming the capability source addition by the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.
@assertion  The capabilities attribute exists and includes a name \"WebSearch\",and the \"sites\" contain the URL \"https://example.com\" in  the declarativeAgent.json file.
Click the "Close (Ctrl+W)" button on the tab for "declarativeAgent.json" in the Visual Studio Code editor to close the file.
Press F1 to open the Command Palette in Visual Studio Code.
Type 'notification:clear All notifications' into the Visual Studio Code command palette at the top of the interface.
Click the “Notifications: Clear All Notifications” command in the Visual Studio Code command palette dropdown.
Press the F1 key to open the Command Palette in Visual Studio Code.
Type 'provision' into the VS Code Command Palette input field, located at the top center of the Visual Studio Code interface.
Click on the "Provision" option under "Microsoft 365 Agents" in the VS Code command palette dropdown to initiate the provisioning process.
Press the F1 key to open the command palette in Visual Studio Code .
Type 'notifications:show notifications' into the VS Code Command Palette input box at the top center of the interface.
Click on the "Notifications: Show Notifications" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette dropdown to select it.
@code wait for #text:/home/vscode/AgentsToolkitProjects/${{var:app_name}}/appPackage/build/manifest.dev.json exist. Timeout: 60s
@assertion notification \"provision stage executed successfully\" exist.
Press F1 to open the command palette in the Visual Studio Code interface with the "Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit" extension panel active.
Type 'notifications:clear all notifications' into the Visual Studio Code command palette input box at the top center of the interface.
Click the "Notifications: Clear All Notifications" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette to initiate clearing notifications.
Press the F1 key to open the command palette in Visual Studio Code.
Type 'add capa' into the VS Code Command Palette input field to search for commands.
Click the "Microsoft 365 Agents: Add Capability" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette dropdown, indicated by the highlighted blue selection bar.
Select the "Web Search" option from the "Add Capability" dropdown in Visual Studio Code, under the prompt "Select a capability source as grounding information for declarative agent."
Click the "Search by URL" option in the "Select Search Type" dropdown menu within Visual Studio Code's command palette interface.
Click the "manifest.json" file option in the "Select Teams manifest_json File" dropdown dialog in Visual Studio Code.
Click the "OK" button in the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit confirmation dialog within the Visual Studio Code application interface.
Click the "Add" button in the overwrite confirmation dialog at the top of the Visual Studio Code interface to proceed with adding new content to the manifest file.
Press Ctrl+P to open the quick file navigation bar at the top of the Visual Studio Code interface.
Type 'declarativeAgent.json' into the VS Code file search input bar at the top center of the interface.
Click on the "declarativeAgent.json" file entry in the VS Code quick open search dropdown to open the file.
@assertion  The capabilities attribute only  include a name \"WebSearch\",and there is no  \"sites\"  attribute present  in  the declarativeAgent.json file.
Press Ctrl+P in Visual Studio Code to open the file quick access panel while editing the declarativeAgent.json file from the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit workspace.
Type 'manifest.json' into the search bar at the top of the Visual Studio Code interface to search for the file within the current project workspace.
Click the "manifest.json" tab in the Visual Studio Code editor to switch to the manifest.json file.
Click the "version" text field in the manifest.json file within Visual Studio Code to edit the app version number ("1.0.0").
Press the left arrow key in the "manifest.json" code editor at line 4, column 23 within Visual Studio Code.
Type text '1' into the "version" field of the manifest.json file in Visual Studio Code, replacing its current value ('1.24').
Save the manifest.json file in Visual Studio Code by pressing Ctrl+S while the file is open and focused in the editor.
Click the "Close" (X) button on the "manifest.json" tab in Visual Studio Code to close the file.
Press the F1 key in Visual Studio Code to open the command palette while editing the declarativeAgent.json file in the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit workspace.
Type 'provision' into the Visual Studio Code command palette search bar to filter available commands related to provisioning in the Microsoft 365 Agents extension.
Click the "Microsoft 365 Agents: Provision" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette, highlighted in blue below the search bar.
Click the "dev" environment option in the "Select an environment" dropdown within Visual Studio Code, under the MICROSOFT 365 AGENTS extension panel.
Press F1 to open the Command Palette in Visual Studio Code while editing the declarativeAgent.json file in the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit workspace.
Type 'notifications:show Notifications' into the Visual Studio Code Command Palette input field at the top of the interface.
Click the "Notifications: Show Notifications" command in the Visual Studio Code command palette.
@assertion notification \"provision stage executed successfully\" exist.
